title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། དབུ་མ། འ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 102)
shelf_note: A Madhyamaka commentary on Mūlamadhyamakakārikā ch. 17 (karma), with MMK 17.29-30 quoted in verse. It belongs in the Derge Tengyur dbu ma section, vol. 'a.

ocr_errors.image: འབྲས་བུ་ཡོད་པར་ག་ལ་འགྱུར (as far as I can read line 5)
ocr_errors.problem: 'མེད་པ་པ' ('nihilist') looks inserted here, probably carried over from the later 'མེད་པ་པ་གཙོ་བོར'. It makes the clause ungrammatical. Neither translation follows it.

ocr_errors.image: no such marks on the block print
ocr_errors.problem: Stray '#' characters are scattered through the transcription. The reader would see them.

tr_errors_A.english: We do not <note>deny</note> karma, the agent, and the result…
tr_errors_A.problem: The page ends at 'as for us, karma, agent, result and so on…'. A adds a negation and a verb that are not on the page, guessing the next page's predicate.
The note guesses the referent; the page does not say what it is the same as or different from.

tr_errors_A.english: starting with the logic that if there is no cause, there is no result and no cause
tr_errors_A.problem: Paraphrases the cited line as an argument rather than marking it as a quotation; the sense is kept.

tr_errors_B.english: Because of that, if one objects: ...
tr_errors_B.problem: 'Because of that' is attached to the reply frame rather than inside the objection. It is a slightly awkward but acceptable reading.

other.note: Translation A renders the first verse line as a markdown heading ('### Because this karma is'), so the reader sees a heading that is not on the page.

pages.prefer_reason: Both are faithful and neither has a serious error, but A invents 'We do not deny' at the page break where B stops honestly at 'we...'.

book_verdict: This is the right leaf, and the transcription is sound apart from stray '#' marks and one apparent insertion ('མེད་པ་པ'). Both English versions are faithful; B is cleaner and A adds a guessed negation at the page break.
